newsitem.title: USA: ING Barings urges overweight in Brazil banks.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings urges overweight in Brazil banks.

text.p: ING Barings' Latin American banks analyst recommended an overweight position in Brazilian banks Wednesday.
The analyst, Nuno Fernandes, said in a telephone conference call Latin American banks had been helped by declining interest rates and economic growth, and the trend was likely to continue.

Among the 23 banks covered by ING Barings, Fernandes recommended a 30 percent allocation for those in Brazil. Argentina received a 20 percent weighting, Chile and Peru 15 percent each, Mexico 12.5 percent and Colombia 2.5 percent.
"The result of this, in our opinion, is an expected total return of 30 percent on our allocation investment by June '98," he said.
Among Fernandes' recommendations and findings from the call and a recent strategy statement:
-- The start of credit growth and recent acquisitions boded well for Brazil. His picks included Banco Credito Nacional and Unibanco, and Banco Itau, which he said is likely "to be a good 1998 story."
-- He forecast strong economic and lending growth in Argentina. Fernandes recommended Banco Frances and Banco de Galicia.
-- In Mexico, Fernandes focused on Grupo Financiero Banorte, since a recent rally left bigger banks fairly valued.
-- Peru remains fundamentally attractive. He recommended Credicorp Ltd and Banco Wiese.
-- In Chile, Fernandes urged concentrating on niche players, such as Banco de A. Edwards.
